review_texts.text: Dalmatian peka — a meal prepared over a fire or ashes, in a pot with a bell-shaped top — is a Croatian culinary tradition, and Dubrava’s expertise in the art has made it one of locals’ favorite restaurants. Under the high bell temperature, meats release and mix juices and aromas, which gives the meal a distinctive flavor. The lamb on the spit is also delicious here, although it likewise takes a lot of time to prepare.

Konoba Dubrava sits in the hills above Dubrovnik, about a 15-minute drive from the Old Town. It is probably the single best argument for renting a car for one evening. The terrace looks out over olive groves and the Adriatic, and the cooking is the definition of what Dalmatian food can be when done with care. The peka here is exceptional. They offer lamb, veal, and octopus versions; the lamb with rosemary and potatoes is the one to order. Call or visit 24 hours in advance, specify your preference, and the family will have it ready.

This gem is actually located outside Dubrovnik, in a village on the mountain that overlooks the city. Konoba Dubrava is known for serving meat dishes that cook for three hours under an iron bell, known locally as peka. To enjoy this local specialty, you must order in advance due to the long cooking time.

If you decide to take the cable car, hike or drive up to Mt. Srd Konoba Dubrava is a great dining option. It’s the perfect place to enjoy traditional Croatian cuisine without the hustle and bustle of the city and tourists in the Old Town, and it even has a playground with a swingset!

review_texts.text: While the Game of Thrones plays out within the walls of the Old Town, on Lapad creative games with Mediterranean flavors are taking place at Pantarul. The restaurant is a favorite of local guests who don’t seek a “table with a view” but rather pleasure and inspiration on the plate. It’s hard to find a better recommendation for local specialties carried out in an innovative and thoughtful way. Their philosophy rests on respect for local ingredients and seasonality, while tradition is honored only by quality. Fresh fish and ingredients from small producers from the Dubrovnik hinterland give every dish a clear local note.

Pantarul is one of the most modern restaurants in Dubrovnik and offers fantastic food. It was started by a local food blogger, Ana-Marija Bujić, along with her husband Milan Vasić, and their friend Đuro Šiljug. Milan and Đuro are a well-known duo in the kithen and they honed their craft in the iconic local restaurants of Nautica, Proto, and Orsan. Top quality here is guaranteed.

We found a nice place nearby that promised some modern Croatian bites and we took a nice walk on the Lapad streets to reach it. Even if it’s location on the side of a busy street was not so appealing at first, the food was really great. They even do some small kids plates, including chicken nuggets with purée that my son ate very well. The name of the place is Pantarul and is definitely worth the trip outside the Dubrovnik old city.

Pantarul is a very popular restaurant in Dubrovnik among locals and tourists alike. It offers casual, bistro-style dining, and fusion food (a play on Italian, French, Croatian, and Asian cuisines). We really wanted to like Pantarul, because we liked their story, playful branding, and casual vibe. We also bought their cookbook and were really excited to taste the food. But we weren’t impressed. We add it here because so many other diners have completely different experiences.

Nakon kratke pauze, od početka ožujka na Lapadu vas očekuje još jedno gastro odredište, Pantarul u kojem možete uživati u delicijama koje se pripremaju prema godišnjim dobima i od namirnica koje vlasnik nabavlja kod lokalnih OPG-ova. Za ponudu koju čine brzi zalogaji i večere od pet sljedova zaslužan je chef Angel van Dammea Mijović.

review_texts.text: 「シュトゥルクリ」や「フジ」など、定番のクロアチア料理をはじめ、 「ロジャータ」や「シュポルキ・マカルリ（ドブロブニク周辺の伝統的なパスタ）」など地元ドブロブニクの伝統的な料理も堪能できます。どちらかと言えば高級店のため、値段設定はちょっとお高いですが味はたしか。きっと満足していただけると思います！クロたびスタッフも今までにたくさんの方におすすめしてきましたが、みなさんから「おいしかった！」「行って良かった！」と大満足のお声を頂戴しました。

It’s recommended that you try and make a reservation at Kopun, especially if you’re visiting Dubrovnik during high season. It’s a very in demand spot! This is probably down to the quality of service and the range of special dishes on offer. All ingredients are freshly sourced and in season, giving you the very best flavor on offer.

When you visit Croatia, you just have to try one of the traditional meals. Thus, the place for you in Dubrovnik is restaurant Kopun. It’s almost as they set a mission for themselves – to save as many old meals and recipes as they can.

Kopun is another one of Dubrovnik’s old town restaurants that we held high hopes for. But it fell short of our expectations. Not as bad though as Pantarul, but still short. The restaurant Kopun is located in a quiet part of the old town, on the top of the Jesuit Stairs, the best known as the filming location of Cersei’s Walk of Shame in the GoT series.

review_texts.text: Lucin Kantun is a hidden gem of Dubrovnik’s gastronomy scene. This small family-owned restaurant is tucked away in a narrow street just off the main street of Dubrovnik – Stradun. Lucin Kantun will pleasantly surprise you with its special approach to preparing well-known traditional dishes. This is the place where love and passion for good food meet with innovative cooking techniques. Come and see what the fuss is all about! Charming interior, beautiful open kitchen, friendly staff, creative cuisine, fresh, high-quality food, and an excellent value for money… are just a few things that made this delightful family-owned restaurant a favorite place for Dubrovnik locals and visitors alike.
Lucin Kantun is one of those hidden gem restaurants in Dubrovnik old town that you’ll be glad you’ve found. It’s authentic and super friendly – and they serve the best lavender gin!
Vratimo se malo u centar gdje ćete biti zadovoljni i ako odaberete Lucin kantun, Sesame i Moskar Street Food.

review_texts.text: In the heart of Dubrovnik's historic center, this intimate, characterful restaurant offers a cuisine with strong Mediterranean and traditional characteristics. The à la carte menu features iconic dishes such as fuži istriani – homemade fresh pasta served with a creamy white sauce of shrimp and mixed mushrooms, enhanced by the aroma of Istrian black truffle. There is also plenty of focus on fish, with both classic and more creative recipes. The selection of Croatian wines is noteworthy.

Set in a peaceful traditional courtyard in the heart of Dubrovnik Old Town, Marco Polo Restaurant is located in the vaulted street Lučarica offering perfect gastro escape from the bustling Dubrovnik summer days. Here you will enjoy typical Dalmatian food combined with new international flavors perfectly matched with the best Croatian Wine.

Odredišta za dobru riblju večeru su restoran Posat, Proto i Orsan, a ako ste ljubitelj košarke i naše velike NBA zvijezde Bojana Bogdanovića otiđite u Forty Four. Restoran koji nosi ime njegovog broja dresa nalazi se u samom centru Grada. Jedan od poznatijih dubrovačkih restorana svakako je i Marco Polo, a novo ime gastro scene je Port 22.

review_texts.text: Moskar Street Food is a small family restaurant in the upper part of Old Town. It is intimate, atmospheric and in my opinion one of the best places to eat real Croatian food. Here I tasted, among other things, a great version of the black risotto, but other Dalmatian dishes are also on the menu. The service is friendly, the portions generous and the flavours pure. You can tell that they cook with love here. It is not a place for extensive dining with lots of fuss, but perfect for those looking for honest dishes in a quiet setting.

Netko je rekao pašticada? Jedno od tradicionalnih jela dubrovačkog kraja uz neizostavne domaće njoke i čašu plavca. Konoba Moskar se nalazi na kultnoj dubrovačkoj ulici Prijeko, koja vrvi restoranima i barovima. ‘Moskar’ znači lepeza ‘po dubrovački’. U ponudi imaju i ‘šporke makarule’ – jelo koje Dubrovčani tradicionalno spravljaju za Festu svetog Vlaha.

review_texts.text: Konoba Tabak is a simple no-frills place that locals love with honest homemade cooking and very affordable prices. Tabak is one of the best places in Dubrovnik to eat a cooked meal on a budget. Tabak serves daily lunches for 8 € to 10 € a dish. Soups cost 3.6 € a portion. Repeat customers get a 25% discount, so plan to eat there every day. The dishes include beans with sausage, grilled mackerels with veggies, rolled veal roast, beer schnitzel, and like. At Tabak, there is also an a la carte menu where prices are equally reasonable.

I’ll be honest, there is very little to say about Tabak’s service, but for the price of otherwise very good food and decent portions, it can be overlooked. With daily marende (late morning snack/meal breaks) and food freshly made on an outdoor grill in front of you while you wait in the shade, Tabak can be a welcome change from the usual hustle and bustle of the city. Tabak has a very relaxed atmosphere and is popular with anyone looking for a good meal.

Konoba Tabak in Gruž is a good example of the format. The menu is short, with daily cooked dishes and a grill, and prices are lower than in the Old Town. The marenda selection changes from day to day: stew, beans, fish, tripe or another cooked dish may appear. It fits naturally into a morning around the Gruž market or a day when you are already passing through the ferry port.

review_texts.text: Among the most sought-after restaurants in the city – reservations are essential – Nautika offers a traditional, rich and well-executed cuisine, with no concessions to passing trends or exotic influences, in which Dalmatian recipes are elevated by solid French and Italian foundations. The service is impeccable, with a well-prepared team and a wine list of excellent calibre. Situated at the entrance to the old city, by the sea, its terraces afford a spectacular view of the Adriatic and the illuminated fortresses of Lovrijenac and Bokar: a venue with a decidedly romantic appeal.

The cuisine is rooted in Mediterranean and Dalmatian traditions while incorporating French and Italian culinary techniques. Local identity comes from the use of Adriatic seafood, while refined presentation reflects fine-dining precision. In addition to two tasting menus, the restaurant offers an à-la-carte selection of starters, soups and main courses. Tuna fillet is paired with dehydrated capers and a trio of fennel, while sea bass arrives with barley, zucchini and an olive-oil-lime emulsion. Among the meat dishes, veal cheeks braised in Dubrovnik Malvasia stand out, served with onion and potato cream, glazed carrots and kale chips.

A very posh restaurant located near the entrance to the Old Town, Nautika boasts a beautiful view of the Lovrijenac and Bokar forts (another King’s Landing site). The location was once a maritime school, and it now features a spectacular terrace and a team of young and ambitious chefs. A titan of Croatian gastronomy, the prices are up there with the quality. This will not be a cheap meal, but for a real splurge, a meal at Nautika is a memorable experience.

One of Dubrovnik’s most prestigious restaurants, Nautika offers two panoramic terraces of starched white-tablecloth formality. Chef Mario Bunda insists on fresh, locally-sourced ingredients. Shellfish star in dishes from shrimp risotto to St. Jacob's scallops, and meat lovers aren't forgotten either, with hearty entrees like veal fillet in wine sauce gracing the menu too.

review_texts.text: A welcoming and informal atmosphere characterises this small restaurant in the very heart of the medieval walls. The menu draws inspiration from Mediterranean tradition while opening to international influences. A selection of Croatian tapas – prosciutto, local cheeses, tartare and tempura – provides the opening, followed by fish, meat and vegetarian dishes, each interpreted with an agreeable contemporary touch. The outdoor seating in a narrow lane of the old town is particularly evocative, perfect for immersing oneself in the magic of Dubrovnik.

People visit the restaurant Zuzori for its beautifully plated dishes, elegant street-side terrace, and modern European and Mediterranean cuisine. The short but varied menu caters even to vegetarians. However, duck breast, oxtail, prawn and sausage croquettes, octopus risotto, and bluefin tuna are the most popular items on Zuzori’s menu. The service is uneven and sometimes slow and clumsy.

U Starom gradu Dubrovniku čeka vas maštovit jelovnik sastavljen od plodova jadranskog mora, salata i tijestenina pripremljen od svježih namirnica. Chef Pasko Kapetanić svoje goste će iznenaditi kombinacijama, načinom pripreme i serviranja. Na meniju restorana našli su se goveđi rep, plavorepa tuna, domaći goveđi burger i dr.

review_texts.text: In the heart of the old city, this establishment, founded in 1886, is a historic venue where guests may take their seats on the outdoor street terrace, in the interior dining room or, the preferred option, on the first-floor terrace. The menu celebrates the local Adriatic catch: the freshest sea bass, king prawns and excellent charcoal grilled octopus, prepared with simplicity and flavour. Alongside the seafood, organic vegetables from local kitchen gardens. Not to be missed is the rožata, the typical crème caramel, a perfect conclusion to an authentic experience in a privileged position.

Restaurant Proto serves exquisite seafood dishes and it is considered one of the best fish restaurants in Dubrovnik. Proto’s fresh seafood, splendid first-floor terrace, and attentive service make Proto one of the most popular restaurants in Dubrovnik among locals and tourists alike. Don’t miss one of Proto’s classic seafood dishes: octopus salad, and freshly caught dentex fish baked with veggies in the oven.

Seafood-oriented Proto claims a tradition dating back to 1886, and it was here that Edward VIII entertained Wallis Simpson in the 1930s. As well as lobster in simple, superbly-balanced sauces, there's fresh shellfish from Mali Ston up the coast. You can spend an enjoyable hour over the fisherman platter for two and the extensive wine list covers just about every quality wine that Croatia has to offer.

review_texts.text: A modest restaurant in a decidedly immodest neighbourhood, close to the exclusive Pucić Palace hotel, offers a simple gastronomic concept that has remained unchanged for decades. As its name suggests, Kamenice specialises are famous oysters from the Mali Ston Bay, served fresh on crushed ice with a slice of lemon. Each day the menu features around fifteen dishes: cheese and prosciutto, black risotto, small fried fish, octopus salad, mussels buzara, fried or grilled squid, omelettes and pasta with prawns. Dessert is always the same – the traditional Dubrovnik rožata. Portions are generous, the fish exceptionally fresh and the prices surprisingly affordable considering the location.

This Dubrovnik classic has been in the same location for decades - right on Gundulićeva Poljana, in the heart of the Old Town. Over all thos decades it has remained practically unchanged, which is a good thing! Modest on the surface, the food is truly excellent. It’s star dishes are the always superb black risotto, small fried fish, octopus salad, and exceedingly fresh oysters. The portions are generous, the fish couldn't be fresher, and the prices are very affordable.

Mjesto pristojnih cijena za plodove mora poput kamenica i mušula (dagnje). Najbolje je početi dan ispijajući kavu sa starijom generacijom Dubrovčana na Gundulićevoj poljani u ovom autohtonom restoranu gdje ćete osjetiti duh prošlosti.

Located in the heart of the old town, Kamenice, meaning oysters in Croatian, is a place to eat just that – oysters! Here you will get the freshest and most reasonably priced oysters in all of Dubrovnik. And, when available, you can also order fried smelt fish. The rest of the menus in’t worth the try.
ただ牡蠣好きの方はここの牡蠣を見て「すごく小っちゃいね～」と目を丸くされていました。・・・が、ここのお店の牡蠣が特別に小さいわけではなく、一般的にクロアチアの牡蠣は日本のものと比べると小ぶりなのです。牡蠣好きの方には、ぜひクロアチアの牡蠣を食していただきたいですが、私のように貝が苦手な方には、このお店ではリゾットやパスタがおすすめ。

review_texts.text: This restaurant right on the waterfront next to the Gruška pjaca (market) is a place where even local fishermen love to eat (always a good sign!). It is a classic Adriatic tavern, with memorabilia and old photos hung on its stone walls, simple tables, and lots of local humor. My favorite dishes: glorijet (fish) platter, tagliatelle with shrimp, catch of the day, veal chops, brunch.

Located next to the fish market, in Dubrovnik’s Gruz neighborhood, Glorijet is the best restaurant in Dubrovnik to eat fresh fish and seafood for an affordable price. Even local fishermen come to eat here! Besides the extensive menu, Glorijet also offers a lunch menu based on a catch of the day, fresh produce from the market (or a butcher!), and the season. Glorijet doesn’t have a terrace, instead, it has a cave-like rustic interior. The place is popular among locals at lunchtime.

Među lokalcima poznat kao najbolje mjesto za marendu u Dubrovniku. Odličan izbor ukusnih lokalnih proizvoda, a pogotovo morskih plodova i ribljih jela. Nude više opcija dnevnih marendi. Morskoj atmosferi dodatno pridonosi interijer restorana koji je smještan unutar tradicionalnog orsana (dio brodogradilišta).

Close to the city market in Gruž harbour you’ll find this lovely old summer residence which has been turned into a bistro where you can enjoy good cooking at sensible prices. Glorijet has earned a reputation among the locals as a good lunch spot.

review_texts.text: Slightly hidden behind the sailing marina in the Lapad area, Orsan is an excellent alternative to the much more famous (and much busier) restaurant of Nautica. It has a fantastic fish menu, everything is fresh and homemade, and you can get your whole lunch for a good price. Locals love it for the excellent service and their brunch menu. While seafood is the star of the show, they do also offer a number of good meat dishes. My favorite dishes: seafood platter Orsan, homemade fish soup, fish of the day, grilled beefsteak, rožata.

Restaurant Orsan is a seafood restaurant with a superb seafront terrace and one of the best Lapad restaurants. A colleague from Dubrovnik invited us for lunch here – a good sign that the restaurant has a good reputation among locals. If you are looking for where to eat in Dubrovnik on a budget, the restaurant also offers a light lunch, for as little as 11 € for a dish. The offer changes daily, and you can see a weekly menu on their Facebook page.

Bar and Restaurant Orsan, located on the edge of the water at a yacht club, is well known for their marende (late morning snack/meal breaks) which are popular among residents and those working on the sea. For a reasonable price one can eat a hearty meal while inspecting local boats and looking across the sparkling water to Mt. Srdj and Gruz.

Restoran smješten usred istoimenog Yacht kluba postao je prepoznatljiv po svježoj ribi, plodovima mora, velikom izboru hrvatskih vina i lijepom okruženju. Za sve koji u ručku ili večeri žele uživati u sjeni borova čekaju jela kao što su hobotnica sa žara (27 €), ražnjići od kozica sa žara (24 €), biftek tagliata (38 €), ribeye odrezak (40 €), vegetarijanski pjat (15 €), dubrovačka rožata (6 €) i dr.

Nestled along the harbor in the Lapad Marina, you won't likely find this seafood spot unless you're looking for it. I come here when I want to have a laid-back lunch by the sea, away from the crowds of the Old Town and Lapad. Orsan serves a variety of local seafood dishes such as black risotto, octopus salad, or salt-baked fish.

review_texts.text: Manu steps lead to Bota Oyster & Sushi bar in Dubrovnik, located inside the oldest part of the city walls, but effort is worth climbing. Charming interior protects in summer heat but the small terrace with only a few high tables, is more vibrant. They prepare in a modern way the freshly caught fish from the southern Adriatic, bluefin tuna, greater amberjack and swordfish, oysters and mussels, as well as local scampi and prawns. With a simple selection of fresh ingredients and Japanese technique, they achieve the harmony and the richness of the taste. Don’t skip the oysters, fresh or tempura. Tuna tartare a la Bota with anchovies, capers, olive oil and tabasco, as well as tuna carpaccio, seasoned only with a little salt and pepper, olive oil and lemon, are superb.

A family-run restaurant with a long tradition, Sushi & Oyster Bar Bota serves fresh seafood in a sleek interior and on a splendid terrace. Esquisite seafood dishes, warm and welcoming staff, lovelyb ambiance, and affordable prices considering the quality of ingredients and the location, make Sushi & Oyster Bar Bota one of the best restaurants in Dubrovnik. It’s also our favorite Dubrovnik old town restaurant. All shellfish, including oysters, come from owner’s shellfish farm in nearby Mali Ston. The food here is simply divine. We could eat at the Bota every day.

Given Dubrovnik’s location on the Adriatic coast, it’s no surprise that seafood is the order of the day at many of the city’s restaurants. But at Bota, they’re serving it mostly in the form of sushi – which makes sense when there’s so much fresh fish available. Bota also specialises in oysters, so order a couple plus a glass of the house Croatian white wine while you ponder the rest of the menu. Particular favourites of ours included the rainbow roll and the “agemaky fantasy” roll, but we also liked the teriyaki steak.

Preko puta dubrovačke katedrale očekuju vas specijaliteti pripremljeni od svježih malostosnkih kamenica te ribe koja dolazi iz Malog mora. U kvalitetu jela uvjeriti ćete se ne samo zbog lijepog izgleda tanjura već i zbog okusa kojeg ćete osjetiti kušajući ih. Komad kamenice ovdje se plaća 4 eura.

review_texts.text: Located in the very center of town, but hidden along the stairs that intersect the old town lies this little gem. In a somewhat tight space, the menu includes fresh ingredients produce which is selected from the market every day and the morning’s catch of seafood. It is more of a snack place than a full sit down restaurant, but its prime location and terrific quality make it a great option should hunger strike while you’re exploring central Dubrovnik’s medieval beauty. My favorite dishes: fried bell peppers, octopus and shrimp burgers, and anchovy and fried calamari sandwiches.

Seafood meets street food at Barba, where you’ll find locals and tourists lining up for some of the city’s most affordable and delicious bites. Vuković notes that it hits all the right marks: a trendy place, awesome seafood, inside the Old Town, quick, and cheap. “The octopus burger is my guilty pleasure,” says Vuković.

Seafood meets street food at Barba, located in Dubrovnik’s Old Town. With limited menu items, this place takes pride in the food and it really shows. The interior is bright, modern and inviting — and the dishes are some of my favorite I had in Dubrovnik.

review_texts.text: Right on the harbour, Lokanda Peskarija has been going strong for donkey’s years and still seems to be popular with locals as well as tourists. They specialise in seafood, so order some octopus salad or grilled squid with garlic butter and a long, cold beer. There’s no better way to celebrate the start of your holiday.

そんな中、 そこそこお手頃価格でおいしいシーフード料理が食べられると評判のレストランが「ロカンダ・ペスカリヤ(Lokanda Peskariija)」。日本のガイドブックでもよく紹介されているお店です。旧港に面した抜群のロケーションでテラス席もあり、夏はいつもたくさんの観光客で賑わっています。このレストランの自慢は鉄鍋に入れたまま出される豪快なシーフード料理。日本人観光客に人気のシーフードリゾットはムール貝や以下、エビがごろごろ入っていてなかなかのお味ですが、エビも殻つきのまま投入されているので、ちょっと食べにくいにが難点。

With a prime location overlooking the harbor in Dubrovnik, Lokanda Peskarija may or may not be a tourist trap. With reviews ranging from spectacular to worst-experience-ever, I was skeptical. We gave it a try one night while craving seafood and outdoor seating — it has plenty of both.

The peskarija (fish market) historically served as the heart of Dalmatian coastal life — as much as any church or town square: deals made, romances kindled, rumours spread, amends made and new arguments born – and fish were sold along the way. Lokanda Peskarija keeps that spirit alive — it sits atop Dubrovnik’s old fish market, just outside the city walls. The open-air restaurant looks over the harbour, where local fishermen set sail in small wooden boats to catch lunch.

review_texts.text: If you only eat one thing in Dubrovnik, make it a cevapi in lepinja from Pile Sandwich Bar. Cevapi are small, skinless grilled minced meat sausages — a staple across the Balkans — and when they're stuffed into a soft lepinja flatbread, it's one of the most satisfying things you'll eat in Croatia. This place is unpretentious, quick, and exactly the kind of spot locals actually go to. It's close to the Pile Gate, which makes it a perfect stop before or after exploring the Old Town.

Sandwich Bar Pile is right at the gate entrance with sandwiches in the €4–9 range. There are no tables inside, but portions are generous, and the bread is fresh. Useful if you need something fast before heading into the heart of Dubrovnik's Old Town.

review_texts.text: Best ice cream in Dubrovnik! Just turn from main street and you'll discover the biggest variety of extremely delicious ice cream. Orange Cheesecake after the breakfast? Pistachio Marzipan Mozart for cloudless weather? Or refreshing Lemon Sorbet after dinner? It's very difficult to make up your mind! Highly recommend!

We are gelato lovers but maaaaan…this one at PEPPINO'S in old town Dubrovnik really kicked everyone else's ass! We bought Pistachio and Hazelnut flavours and oh my god they were amazing! Small chunks of pistachio and hazelnut inside, suuuper creamy and smooth… what can I say more… My mouth is drooling as I write this – I think I'm gonna head back there and order another one. Prices are very, very ok and staff was very friendly.

メニューにはクリーミー系のジェラートと、ソルベ系の乳製品不使用のヴィーガンメニューがありました。暑かったのでソルベ系も気になったのですが、まずは王道！と思い、クリーミー系の方から、ヨーグルト＆ベリー（3ユーロ）を選びました！1フレーバー3ユーロだったのですが、なかなかの大盛りジェラートでした！物価は高いのに、ジェラートが安いのはイタリアでもクロアチアでもうれしいポイントですね！買ったあと、気が付いたらお店の前に大行列ができていました。
Peppino's Gelato Shops — multiple locations, Old Town & Ploče Gate. Amazing gelato flavors that locals rave about.

review_texts.text: たくさんのアイスクリーム屋さんが点在するドブロブニク旧市街。1軒1軒食べ歩きをするのも楽しいですが、地元民にも「おいしい！」と評判なのが、プラツァ通りのサイドストリートに位置するドルチェ・ヴィータ(Dolce Vita)。細い石畳の路地にあるテラス席は、いつもスイーツを楽しむ地元民や観光客であふれています。人気はもちろんアイスクリームですが、パフェやパラチンケ（クロアチア風クレープ）もあります。アイスクリームの種類は20種類以上！

続いて2軒目は、ストラドゥン通りから1歩入ったところにある、ガイドさんおすすめのスイーツショップ「Dolce Vita」にも行ってみました。こちらはジェラートだけではなく、パンケーキにアイスをトッピングしているメニューもありました。ドブロブニクの地元の女子たちもスイーツを食べようという時には、ここのお店に来るのが定番なんだそうです。店内はとても忙しそうで、プレートデザートを注文して店内で食べている方が多く、店内の席も外のテラス席も満席状態でした。
This colourful little spot does great cakes, muffins and ice cream – among the best in town – just off Stradun.

review_texts.text: If you take coffee seriously, Cogito is your place. Tucked inside Dubrovnik's Old Town, it's one of the few spots in the city where trained baristas actually know what they're doing — flat whites, espressos, cold brew, Chemex — all executed properly. In a city where mediocre coffee is the norm, Cogito stands out immediately. It's small and can get busy, but it's worth seeking out. Particularly good after a walk along the city walls when you need something that actually tastes like coffee rather than warm brown water.

In an arched passageway near the maritime museum, this cute semi-hidden gem is the place to go for people who are serious about their coffee. With beans supplied by the Cogito coffee-roasting outfit in Zagreb, the cuppas that come out of this place are reliably strong, full of flavour and carefully prepared by a trained barista. The place itself is tiny, but seats outside on the cobbles make it an altogether charming place to recharge.

As you might expect from a coffee specialist they spread their net rather wider than the average Croatian kafić, with trained baristas serving up smooth espressos as well as grappling with the demands of filter, Chemex and cold-brew coffees.

review_texts.text: One of Dubrovnik's most iconic cafe settings. Arsenal sits right on Luža Square in the heart of the Old Town — established in 1895, it's been serving coffee to locals and visitors for over a century. The terrace looks out over the square with views of St. Blaise Church, Sponza Palace, and the Orlando Column. From the eastern terrace you can see the Old City Harbour framed by St. John's Fortress. It's not the cheapest option and it's always busy — but for a coffee with one of the best views in Dubrovnik, it earns its place. The almond cream cake is reportedly excellent if you want something to go with it.

review_texts.text: We personally like D’Vino Wine Bar the most out of all the wine bars in Dubrovnik. When in Dubrovnik, we always stop by for a glass of wine or two. D’Vino has a great location, a cozy atmosphere, friendly and wine-educated staff, interesting snack platters, and a great choice of Croatian wines by the glass. A glass of wine will easily set you back 8 €. And this is the only drawback with D’Vino.

Dubrovnik’s first real wine bar is run by a friendly and knowledgeable team. D’Vino manages to stock more than 100 varieties, most of them available by the glass. Every decent Istrian, Slavonian and Dalmatian label is here, including Grgić Plavac Mali and Zlatan Plavac. The house wine begins at 25kn and savoury meat-and-cheese platters are tailor-made to complement. It’s a comfortable, modern, intimate space to enjoy a drink – with a few seats outside in summer.

Gdje probati najbolja vina koja se nude na čašu uz obavezni tasting? D’vino wine bar skriven je u jednoj od uličica kraj Straduna. Točnije u Palmotićevoj ulici, preko puta Glam caffe i beer bar. Kako vole reći – vino je super, ali nekad treba probati i pivo. Kušajte ‘Hrvatsku u čaši’. Nude vina od malih proizvođača od Slavonije, preko Istre do Dalmacije.

If you’re looking for a shady spot for a glass of wine and some local snacks at aperitivo o’clock, look no further than D’vino – a wine bar nestled up one of the flights of stairs that lead off the main drag in the Old Town. They serve plenty of Croatian wines (as well as international vino) by the glass and bottle, plus some cheeses, olives and other nibbles.

review_texts.text: M'Arden is a wine bar up a few staircases south of the Stradun, roughly towards the ethnographic museum (in a former granary storage warehouse, and in flux this summer) where you will find a raised terrace covered in a pergola with grapevines and leafy trees. Local reviewer says this: "Zen garden in the heart of the Old city. Calm and cozy place to escape the world. Staff is welcoming and well educated," Have a charcuterie plate with a glass of wine. On my recent visit in late May, I was trying every version of Travarica that I could, and theirs was good, but they had an Istrian amaro that was excellent.

U malenoj oazi unutar grada, na adresi Ulica od Domina 8 smjestio se wine bar M’arden. Ovo mjesto nudi jedinstvenu selekciju vrhunskih vina i pića, upotpunjenu hranom koja je istovremeno jednostavna i kompleksna, puna okusa i tekstura.

Hidden within Dubrovnik’s city walls, M’arden is a leafy oasis where romance, wine and flavour come together. By day, sip coffee in the shade of plane trees or relax with a glass of Croatian wine after exploring the Old Town. As evening falls, linger over exquisite bites and guided tastings that showcase the country’s finest regions.

review_texts.text: Beside Dubrovnik Cathedral with its glittering treasury, Bura Bistro & Bar is a recently opened top spot in the historic Old Town serving sensational seasonal food, innovative wines and quality cocktails. Named after an Adriatic wind, Bura is overseen and co-owned by professional sommelier Marin, who has travelled the globe inspired by good food. Bura’s concise menu changes throughout the year, underscored by the long-standing relationship Marin and his team have developed with local farmers and producers. The daily catch is just that, fresh fish and seafood arriving every morning from the Adriatic lapping close by. In summer, tapas-style dishes come into their own, most notably ceviche, here prepared with authentic expertise.

For a modern take on Croatian food, be sure to head to Bura Bistro. You’ll find it directly behind the beautiful Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary and the menu will make your mouth water just by looking at it. Be warned however, the plate sizes are large, so you won’t really need to order too much to be full. Although, you might want to keep eating, such are the flavours!

Behind the Cathedral of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary you can find Bura Bistro. Nestled into one corner of a gorgeous plaza that is filled with other dining establishments, this place came highly recommended to us and they delivered. We only ordered two appetizers on this evening, but from the presentation and flavour we can’t wait to return to Dubrovnik to try more of their dishes.

review_texts.text: If you’re looking to try out some of Croatia’s most delicious wines – and have a few snacks on the side too – then the Bakus Wine Bar is the atmospheric little spot for you! review_texts.text: Despite the name, the Taj Mahal's cuisine pays homage to Bosnia and Balkan traditions. In the heart of Dubrovnik's Old Town, this restaurant is a landmark for those seeking authentic, rich and tantalizing flavours served in a convivial and unpretentious atmosphere. The extensive and varied menu simply tells the story of Bosnian culinary tradition: a couple of pages are devoted to traditional dishes, alongside tasty grilled meats (from their own butcher shop), flavourful vegetables, and specialities prepared according to family recipes. Not to be missed is the homemade plum baklava made by the owner's mother – a real treat.

Taj Mahal first started as a tiny venue in the Old Town of Dubrovnik, where the owners, a young married couple Edin and Edina, shared their passion for Bosnian cuisine. Inviting smell spreading from the grill and stove in their Old Town restaurant is very popular with both locals and tourists ever since their opened a door back in 2004. Čevapi, Burek, Begova čorba, Klepe (Bosnian minced meat dumplings), Dolma, are just some of the dishes that will take you to the heaven of taste.

Despite its name, the restaurant Taj Mahal serves traditional Bosnian dishes, and it is one of the most popular restaurants in Dubrovnik. The small interior gets busy quickly. Although Taj Mahal serves some vegetarian options (e.g. filo pastry with spinach), this is a mecca for meat lovers. There is another Taj Mahal restaurant within Hotel Lero in the Lapad area. It's run by the same owners and has the same concept.

・営業時間：公式サイト・在住ガイド記事に記載がない店は Wanderlog 経由の Google 掲載時間（2026年9月＝シーズン中の値）を使用し hours に明記。5月は短縮営業の可能性あり、要再確認。Nautika・Proto・Lokanda Peskarija は冬季休業の季節営業（5月は営業期）。
・営業中の根拠：ミシュラン2026（datePublished 2026-06-25）、Dubrovnik Online（2026-09-16更新・『2026年9月に営業状況を確認』と明記）、Journal.hr 2025-07-10、CroTabi（在住日本人ガイド）2025-01、Rick Steves フォーラム 2026-06 等。公式SNSの日付つき投稿は Instagram/Facebook がログイン壁で未確認。
・乳児連れ：クロアチアの小規模店はハイチェアが少ない（Chasing the Donkey 在住者の子連れ記事）。旧市街はストラドゥン以外ほぼ階段で、ベビーカーより抱っこ紐推奨（stroller-friendly.com / 家族ブログ）。ラパド（Pantarul・Orsan）は平坦で移動しやすい。個別店でハイチェアを明記した出典は見つからず、kids タグは付与していない。
・評価割れ：Pantarul・Kopun（Frank about Croatia が辛口）、Lokanda Peskarija（Travels and Treats が『観光客向けか微妙』）、Kamenice（牡蠣以外は評価割れ）、Zuzori（サービスのむら）。いずれも review_texts に原文を併記。
・Malvasija Wine Bar は Google 上『閉業』表示のため除外（運営者の閉店告知は未確認）。代替に Bakus Wine Bar。DBC（クラフトビール）は営業状況不明で除外。
・写真：Glorijet・Konoba Tabak・Bakus は取得可能な実写画像が見つからず空配列。Wanderlog の Google 写真は使っていない。
・読めなかった情報源：TripAdvisor/Restaurant Guru（規則で不使用）、Forbes（403）、Travels and Treats（403・Wanderlog 引用のみ）、Washington Post（接続不可・Wanderlog 引用のみ）、Coast to Coast Newspaper（403）、tinytravelship（403）、Gault&Millau の Dubrovnik 一覧（JS描画で店名取得不可・個別ページは可）、dubrovackapivovara.hr（Page not found）、Glorijet の eatbu 公式（404）、Instagram/Facebook。

dubrovnik_B.json: 担当: casual / sweets / outside（ドブロブニク）。WebSearch 使用 21 回。読めなかった情報源: lostindubrovnik.com（大半のページがSiteGround captchaで遮断、2ページのみ取得）、hrvatskekarta.com（403）、HappyCow（空応答）、Fodor's・Frommer's（403）、guide.michelin.com の一覧ページ（JS描画で店名取得不可。個別ページは可）、eatbu（Glorijet公式予約ページ404）、holyburek の Dubrovnik 店舗詳細住所（ストアロケーターは都市名のみ）。Instagram/Facebook は未読のため、多くの店で 2025〜26 年の公式日付つき投稿は未確認（status に『要確認』と明記）。乳児連れ情報は出典に明記が乏しく、ほぼ全店『未確認』。Spaghetteria Toni はキッズメニューあり、Pizzeria Tabasco は屋根つきテラス・宿への無料配達あり。Taj Mahal はミシュランがより広いLapadのHotel Lero店を案内しており、ベビーカー連れならLero店も候補。5月の営業時間: Tabasco は冬季ダイヤ（5月は無休 10-23時）、Spaghetteria Toni は日曜休。
